title: Ezekiel Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 28.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 28, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came again unto me
Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus
Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God?
They shall bring thee down to the pit
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came again unto me
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in the chapter, found in Ezekiel 28:1.

questions.question: Who is the message in Ezekiel 28 addressed to?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus', as found in Ezekiel 28:2.

questions.question: What has the prince of Tyrus said regarding his status?
options: I sit in the seat of men
I am the prince of the seas
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the prince has said, 'I am a God', as stated in Ezekiel 28:2.

questions.question: What does the Lord GOD say about the heart of the prince of Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'thine heart is lifted up', as found in Ezekiel 28:2.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel, who is wiser than Daniel?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'thou art wiser than Daniel', in Ezekiel 28:3.

questions.question: What has the prince of Tyrus gained through his wisdom?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that he 'with thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches', found in Ezekiel 28:4.

questions.question: What has caused the heart of the prince of Tyrus to be lifted up?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches', as found in Ezekiel 28:5.

questions.question: What will happen to the prince of Tyrus according to the Lord GOD?
options: He will be brought down to the pit
questions.correctAnswer: He will be brought down to the pit
questions.explanation: The text states, 'I will bring strangers upon thee... They shall bring thee down to the pit', as found in Ezekiel 28:7-8.

questions.question: What shall the prince of Tyrus die the deaths of?
questions.explanation: The verse states he shall 'die the deaths of them that are slain', as found in Ezekiel 28:8.

questions.question: What question does the Lord pose to the prince of Tyrus?
options: Wilt thou yet say I am a God?
questions.correctAnswer: Wilt thou yet say I am a God?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly asks, 'Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God?', as found in Ezekiel 28:9.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 28, who is ultimately in control over the prince of Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The entire chapter indicates God's authority over the situation, especially in verse 9 where it is stated that he shall be in the hand of him that slayeth thee.

questions.question: The prince of Tyrus considers himself to be what?
questions.explanation: The text states that the prince has said, 'I am a God', indicating he considers himself to be divine, as seen in Ezekiel 28:2.

questions.question: The wisdom of the prince of Tyrus is compared to that of Daniel.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:3 states 'thou art wiser than Daniel', confirming this comparison.

questions.question: The prince of Tyrus will be lifted up because of his humility.
questions.explanation: The text states that his heart is lifted up because of his riches, not humility, as found in Ezekiel 28:5.

questions.question: The Lord promises prosperity to the prince of Tyrus.
questions.explanation: The Lord's message is one of judgment and decline, not prosperity, particularly in Ezekiel 28:7-8.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the king of Tyrus according to Ezekiel 28:10?
options: He will die the deaths of the uncircumcised
He will become a great ruler
He will be restored to power
questions.correctAnswer: He will die the deaths of the uncircumcised
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ezekiel 28:10, which says, 'Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:8 promise will happen if someone does what verse 28:7 commands?
options: They will be brought down to the pit
questions.correctAnswer: They will be brought down to the pit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:8 states, 'They shall bring thee down to the pit,' indicating the consequence of defiance against God.

questions.question: What description is given of the king of Tyrus in Ezekiel 28:12?
options: He is full of wisdom and perfect in beauty
He will be a great warrior
He is a servant of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: He is full of wisdom and perfect in beauty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:12 describes the king as 'Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:14 reveal about the king of Tyrus's status?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:14 states, 'Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 28:15, what was found in the king of Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:15 mentions, 'till iniquity was found in thee,' indicating the presence of pride and sin.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Ezekiel 28:16 for the king's sin?
options: He will be cast out of the mountain of God
questions.correctAnswer: He will be cast out of the mountain of God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:16 states, 'therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:17 say about the king's heart?
options: It was lifted up because of beauty
questions.correctAnswer: It was lifted up because of beauty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:17 states, 'Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty,' indicating pride.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 28:18 describe the king's actions?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:18 says, 'Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:3 say about the king's wisdom?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:3 states, 'Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 28:5, why was the king's heart lifted up?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:5 states, 'thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:9 imply about the king's attitude toward death?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:9 states, 'Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God?' indicating a false sense of divinity.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be drawn from Ezekiel 28:10 about humility in leadership?
options: Leaders should seek to gather riches
Leaders should boast of their wisdom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:10 emphasizes the consequences of pride, reminding leaders to remain humble.

questions.question: Is it true that pride can lead to downfall according to the message in Ezekiel 28?
questions.explanation: The passage illustrates how the king's pride led to his downfall, especially in verses like Ezekiel 28:17.

questions.question: Is it false that the king of Tyrus was known for his humility and service?
questions.explanation: The text shows that the king's heart was lifted up, indicating pride rather than humility (Ezekiel 28:17).

questions.question: Is it false that the king of Tyrus had a perfect character from the beginning?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:15 indicates that iniquity was found in him, suggesting imperfection in character.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 28.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 28:19, what will happen to those who know the subject among the people?
options: They shall be astonished at thee
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be astonished at thee
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:19 states 'All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee,' indicating astonishment is the reaction.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 28:22, what is the purpose of the LORD being glorified in the midst of Zidon?
options: So they shall know that I am the LORD
So the people will worship Zidon
questions.correctAnswer: So they shall know that I am the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:22 says, 'they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall have executed judgments in her,' indicating the purpose is for recognition of the LORD.

questions.question: What judgment is prophesied against Zidon in Ezekiel 28:23?
options: Pestilence and blood in her streets
questions.correctAnswer: Pestilence and blood in her streets
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:23 specifically mentions, 'I will send into her pestilence, and blood into her streets,' indicating the type of judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 28:24, what imagery is used to describe those who despised Israel?
options: A pricking brier and grieving thorn
A roaring lion and ravenous wolf
A burning fire and smoking furnace
A slippery serpent and venomous viper
questions.correctAnswer: A pricking brier and grieving thorn
questions.explanation: Verse 24 uses 'there shall be no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel, nor any grieving thorn' to describe the enemies.

questions.question: What will happen when the house of Israel is gathered from among the people according to Ezekiel 28:25?
options: They shall dwell in their land given to Jacob
They shall build a great city
questions.correctAnswer: They shall dwell in their land given to Jacob
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:25 says, 'then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob,' indicating their return and dwelling.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 28:26, what condition allows Israel to dwell safely and with confidence?
options: When God has executed judgments upon those that despise them
When Israel conquers their enemies by force
When they build a strong army
When they form alliances with surrounding nations
questions.correctAnswer: When God has executed judgments upon those that despise them
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states, 'when I have executed judgments upon all those that despise them round about them; and they shall know that I am the LORD their God,' linking safety to God's judgment.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'pestilence' (Ezekiel 28:23) mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word translated as 'pestilence' in Ezekiel 28:23 (דֶּבֶר, dever) refers to a plague or deadly disease, commonly used in the Old Testament to describe divine judgment.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 28:12-19 where the king of Tyrus is described?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:12-19 uses typology, portraying the king of Tyrus as a figure resembling the ideal anointed cherub and Eden imagery, symbolizing pride and fall, foreshadowing Satan's fall.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the pride and fall theme of Ezekiel 28:2-10?
questions.explanation: Luke 10:18 refers to seeing 'Satan fall like lightning from heaven,' echoing the pride and fall theme in Ezekiel 28:2-10 about the prince of Tyrus exalted and then cast down.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse is a cross-reference for the promise of Israel dwelling safely in Ezekiel 28:25-26?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 30:5 promises God will bring the scattered Israelites back into their land, paralleling the gathering and dwelling safely in Ezekiel 28:25-26.

questions.question: What verse precedes Ezekiel 28:19, describing the fire that will devour the cherub?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:18 directly precedes 28:19 and describes the fire from the cherub's midst that will devour him, setting the scene for verse 19's astonishment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'prince of Tyrus' claiming 'I am a God' in Ezekiel 28:2 in its historical context?
options: It reflects royal hubris and blasphemy threatening divine order
It indicates a literal claim to deity accepted by the people
It is a metaphor for political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects royal hubris and blasphemy threatening divine order
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:2 shows the prince's hubris in setting his heart as the heart of God, a blasphemous overreach historically understood as pride leading to downfall.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the structure of Ezekiel 28:12-19, where the king of Tyrus is depicted with Eden and cherub imagery?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:12-19 is framed by references to perfection and downfall, using inclusio to bracket the description of the king with Eden and cherub imagery, emphasizing the theme of pride and judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 28:15 connect with the concept of original perfection and subsequent fall in biblical theology?
options: It states the cherub was perfect until iniquity was found in him
It describes the creation of the world
It commands Israel to build altars
It foretells the coming of the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: It states the cherub was perfect until iniquity was found in him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:15 emphasizes the cherub's original perfection and subsequent corruption by sin, paralleling theological themes of original creation and fall.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 28:24 states that the house of Israel will continue to experience grief and oppression from surrounding nations.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:24 states there shall be no more a pricking brier or grieving thorn to the house of Israel from those that despised them, indicating an end to such oppression.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 28:2 teach about human sin in relation to pride and self-exaltation?
options: Human pride leads to an erroneous claim of divinity, highlighting man's created nature and limits
Human beings can become gods by setting their heart as the heart of God
Pride is a virtue that elevates man to God’s status
Self-exaltation is tolerated by God if accompanied by wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride leads to an erroneous claim of divinity, highlighting man's created nature and limits
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:2 shows the prince of Tyrus claiming 'I am a God,' but God corrects him, emphasizing he is 'a man, and not God,' demonstrating the sin of pride and false self-exaltation.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is revealed in Ezekiel 28:7?
options: God brings foreign nations as instruments of judgment against human arrogance
God never uses other nations in His plans
Divine judgment is always hidden and never visible
God forgives all arrogance without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God brings foreign nations as instruments of judgment against human arrogance
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:7 declares that God will bring 'strangers...the terrible of the nations' to judge the prince of Tyrus, showing God's sovereignty in using nations to execute judgment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 28:15 teach about the doctrine of original righteousness and the entrance of sin?
options: Created beings were originally perfect but fell when iniquity was found
Created beings were sinful from their inception
Sin is inherent and cannot be separated from creation
Perfection and sin coexist in created beings
questions.correctAnswer: Created beings were originally perfect but fell when iniquity was found
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:15 states, 'Thou wast perfect...till iniquity was found in thee,' affirming the doctrine that creation began in righteousness and perfection but was marred by sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 28:16 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:16 speaks of God casting out the 'covering cherub' for sin, demonstrating God's holiness and intolerance of sin within His presence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly revealed in Ezekiel 28:22?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 28:22, God declares 'I am against thee, O Zidon,' showing His sovereign authority over nations and His power to execute judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 28:13 connect to the broader biblical theme of the fall of Satan as portrayed in Isaiah 14 and Revelation 12?
options: It presents a portrayal of a being originally perfect and adorned before fall, aligning with the narrative of Satan's fall
It denies the existence of any angelic beings
It teaches that Satan was never created perfect
It equates Satan with a human king without spiritual implications
questions.correctAnswer: It presents a portrayal of a being originally perfect and adorned before fall, aligning with the narrative of Satan's fall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:13 describes precious stones and beauty in Eden, paralleling Isaiah 14 and Revelation 12's depiction of the fall of a once-exalted angelic being.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 28:24-26 prepare for the eschatological restoration theme found in the New Testament?
options: It foretells Israel’s regathering and sanctification, prefiguring ultimate restoration in Christ
It suggests Israel will be permanently scattered
It condemns Israel without hope of return
It focuses only on immediate historical events without future implications
questions.correctAnswer: It foretells Israel’s regathering and sanctification, prefiguring ultimate restoration in Christ
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:24-26 promises Israel's gathering and sanctification, which anticipates the New Testament theme of restoration through Christ’s redemptive work.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 28:12 and Ezekiel 28:14 teach about the nature of created perfection and angelic roles?
options: Created beings can be perfect in wisdom and beauty and have appointed roles like the anointed cherub
Angelic beings are inherently sinful and unclean
Created beings are not given special roles or honor
questions.correctAnswer: Created beings can be perfect in wisdom and beauty and have appointed roles like the anointed cherub
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:12 describes perfection in wisdom and beauty, and 28:14 identifies the being as 'the anointed cherub,' indicating roles assigned by God to perfect created beings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 28:17 and Ezekiel 28:18 teach about the consequences of sin and divine judgment?
options: Pride and corruption lead to destruction and public humiliation by God’s judgment
Divine judgment is private and hidden
Sin is overlooked if accompanied by beauty
Corruption does not affect divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and corruption lead to destruction and public humiliation by God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:17 speaks of lifted-up heart and corrupted wisdom, and 28:18 describes defilement and fire judgment, illustrating consequences of sin under divine justice.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Ezekiel 28:5 and Ezekiel 28:6 provide about the relationship between wisdom, riches, and pride?
options: Wisdom and riches can lead to pride, which results in divine judgment
Wisdom always leads to humility and blessing
Pride is unrelated to material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom and riches can lead to pride, which results in divine judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:5 shows heart lifted up because of riches gotten by wisdom, and 28:6 pronounces judgment because of setting heart as God’s, linking riches and pride with judgment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Ezekiel 28:12-19 is merely a human king’s lament without spiritual significance. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It reveals a dual-layered oracle addressing both a human ruler and a spiritual being, illustrating the fall of an exalted angelic figure
It only concerns a human king’s political downfall
It denies any angelic or spiritual dimension
It is a poetic exaggeration with no doctrinal content
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals a dual-layered oracle addressing both a human ruler and a spiritual being, illustrating the fall of an exalted angelic figure
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:12-19 uses symbolic language about Eden, precious stones, and cherubim that transcend a mere human king, teaching about spiritual pride and fall.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 28:3 teach about divine omniscience as it relates to human wisdom?
options: Human wisdom, even as great as Daniel’s, is limited compared to God’s omniscience
Human wisdom can rival God’s knowledge
Secret things are hidden from God but revealed to men
Divine omniscience is irrelevant to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Human wisdom, even as great as Daniel’s, is limited compared to God’s omniscience
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:3 acknowledges great human wisdom but implicitly contrasts it with God’s greater knowledge, underscoring divine omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 28:9 regarding God's response to human arrogance?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:9 shows that despite arrogance, the prince will be judged and remain a man under the hand of the one who slays him, exhibiting God's justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 28:20-23 contribute to the biblical narrative of God’s judgment on idolatrous nations?
options: It portrays God actively opposing and punishing Zidon, reflecting consistent biblical themes of judgment on idolaters
It endorses idolatry by showing God's indifference
It ignores the fate of surrounding nations
It suggests idolatry will be ultimately victorious
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays God actively opposing and punishing Zidon, reflecting consistent biblical themes of judgment on idolaters
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:20-23 describes God’s judgment on Zidon for opposition to Israel, consistent with biblical judgment against idolaters.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 28:8 and Ezekiel 28:10 teach about the fate of the proud and unrepentant?
options: They will experience death at the hands of strangers, illustrating divine judgment on the uncircumcised
They will be preserved despite their sin
They will be exalted to divine status
questions.correctAnswer: They will experience death at the hands of strangers, illustrating divine judgment on the uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 28:8 and 28:10 describe death by strangers and the death of the uncircumcised as a result of pride and sin, showing divine judgment.
